free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 with '10k credits per month'. One shared monthly pool across every product, with the vendor's own per-product rates: 'Text to Speech 1 credit per character; Speech to Text 330 credits per minute; Eleven Music 900 credits per minute; Sound Effects 200 credits per generation; Voice Changer and Voice Isolator 1,000 credits per minute'. 10,000 credits therefore buys either 10,000 characters of TTS (about 10 minutes of audio at the common 1,000 characters a minute), or 30 minutes of speech-to-text, or 50 sound effects, or 5 minutes of voice isolation, per month.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: the 10,000 credits compose with a free transcription service by splitting the job: send speech-to-text to a vendor with a larger minute allowance and keep ElevenLabs for the TTS voice, because 330 credits a minute makes this pool the worst value as a transcriber. What breaks: any loop that synthesises more than 10,000 characters a month, which is roughly 10 minutes of speech.

limits.value: the monthly credit pool is small and does not roll over on the Free plan: 'Rollover does not apply to the Free plan', so the 10,000 credits are lost at the end of each billing cycle and a batch job larger than 10 minutes of audio cannot be finished across two months.

'Text to Speech 1 credit per character; Speech to Text 330 credits per minute; Eleven Music 900 credits per minute; Sound Effects 200 credits per generation; Voice Changer and Voice Isolator 1,000 credits per minute', quoted from the FAQ 'How many credits does each product use?'

record.notes: These are inference credits, not general compute: no machine, no shell, no GPU is handed over, only metered calls to a hosted voice model. Per-month character cost of the cheapest paid lane for scale: Starter at USD 6 for 30,000 credits is USD 0.20 per 1,000 characters. Open question: whether one email address can hold more than one free workspace; the pricing page does not say and no probe was run against the signup endpoint.

record.category: text-to-speech and speech-to-text API, monthly free credit pool

free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 with 10,000 credits per month, no credit card required. One shared monthly pool across every product: Text to Speech 1 credit per character on multilingual models (0.5 to 1 credit per character on Flash and Turbo through the API), Speech to Text 330 credits per minute, Eleven Music 900 credits per minute, Sound Effects 200 credits per generation. Free-plan API access is included; the pool resets each billing cycle and does not roll over.
free_tier.notes: models on the API pricing page: text-to-speech Eleven v4, v4 Turbo, v3 and Flash/Turbo families, speech-to-text Scribe v2 and Scribe v2 Realtime, music, sound effects, voice changer and voice isolator. unverified: which of these models the Free plan can call through the API, because the pages read list the Free column only as a credit count

record.interface_detail: HTTP and WebSocket requests from any language; official Python and Node.js libraries
record.tooling: official Python (pip install elevenlabs) and Node.js (@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js) libraries, or raw HTTP and WebSocket with an API key created in the account settings
record.chaining: 10,000 credits a month is about 10,000 characters of text-to-speech, enough for short voice-over or a TTS smoke test inside a free CI job; the speech-to-text rate of 330 credits per minute makes this pool poor value for transcription, so send transcription to a service with a larger allowance and keep this pool for the voice.

The gate is a company: 'The ElevenLabs Grants program is open to all startups or companies with less than 25 employees', 'Only applications with valid business emails will be considered', 'Agencies, consulting firms and SMBs are not eligible', 'One application per company', and the programme requires 'a business or monetization strategy' with 'No short-term or one-off projects'.

record.chaining: 33M characters at 1 credit a character is 33,000 minutes of TTS, and the vendor prices that against its own Pro tier: 600,000 credits for USD 99, so 33M credits is about 55 months of Pro. What breaks: the award, not the quota. No chain makes an unapproved application usable.

limits.value: a review committee decides: the grant is applied for and approved 'in our sole discretion', so a person with an email address alone holds a company-shaped application with no product to show; the 33M characters are unreachable without a company, a business email domain and a monetisation story.

record.notes: These are inference credits, not general compute. Classified as a refutation: the largest per-person voice credit in this market is not reachable by a person. An applicant would need a registered company, a domain email and a product with a monetisation strategy, and even then the decision is discretionary. The value claim of 'USD 5,500+' is the vendor's own arithmetic, not measured.
